answer: If an agent bids below its optimal value in CIRCA, it receives worse utility compared to if it had followed its optimal bidding strategy. Specifically, the utility gained by the agent decreases when it deviates from its optimal bid, as it becomes less likely to win the premium reward and risks losing the value from deployment if the bid does not reach the price of compliance. Thus, bidding below the optimal value results in a lower expected utility for the agent.
